Builder confidence hits 14 year low for single-family homes
November 19, 2026 | 7:52 am CST
Builder confidence hits 14 year low for single-family homes

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Builder confidence has dropped to a 14-year low, dragged down by high mortgage rates, ongoing inflation pressure, elevated energy and material costs, rising labor shortages and hesitant buyers.

Builder confidence in the market for newly built single-family homes fell four points to 25 in November, according to the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (HMI). The reading was the lowest since April 2012.

The housing market faces a range of supply-side challenges, including building material costs pushed higher by tariffs, an ongoing shortage of construction workers and excessive regulations that undermine housing affordability. Stepped up immigration enforcement is affecting labor availability in some markets. Higher fuel prices are prompting subcontractors to raise their rates. Mortgage rates above 7%, softer consumer confidence and an uncertain economic outlook are holding buyers back. Consequently, single-family home builders are pulling back on construction volumes.

In November, 46% of builders reduced prices, the highest share in the post-Covid period, according to the latest HMI survey. The average price reduction held at 6% for an eighth straight month. Meanwhile, 68% of builders offered sales incentives, also a post-Covid high, marking the 20th consecutive month in which at least 60% of builders used them.

Derived from a monthly survey that NAHB has been conducting for more than 40 years, the NAHB/Wells Fargo HMI gauges builder perceptions of current single-family home sales and sales expectations for the next six months as “good,” “fair” or “poor.” The survey also asks builders to rate traffic of prospective buyers as “high to very high,” “average” or “low to very low.” Scores for each component are then used to calculate a seasonally adjusted index where any number over 50 indicates that more builders view conditions as good than poor.

All three of the major HMI indices posted losses in November. The index measuring current sales conditions fell six points to 28, the index gauging future sales expectations dropped two points to 30 and the index charting prospective buyer traffic fell two points to 16 – its lowest level in 15 years, excluding the start of the pandemic in 2020.

Looking at the three-month moving averages for regional HMI scores, the Northeast dropped four points to 34, the Midwest fell five points to 35, the South fell three points to 27 and the West posted a three-point decline to 23. The HMI tables can be found at nahb.org/hmi.
